interest: Rebuilding the Japanese Red Cross under SCAP, with its 1947 Junior Red Cross handbook.
overview: This file (State Department decimal file 894.142) documents U.S. government oversight and policy regarding the Japanese Red Cross from February 1945 to April 1948, spanning the close of World War II and the Allied Occupation of Japan. The collection begins with a wartime cross-reference sheet noting civilian message routes permitted across Japanese-occupied territories, followed by a December 1945 SWNCC memorandum advising General Douglas MacArthur to weigh wartime misuse of the Japanese Red Cross when deciding whether to authorize Japanese attendance at an International Red Cross conference. The remainder of the file centers on an April 1948 diplomatic despatch from the U.S. Political Adviser in Tokyo enclosing the complete text of a September 1947 SCAP-approved handbook for reorganizing the Japanese Junior Red Cross into an instrument of democratic education, community hygiene, and international friendship, along with subsequent correspondence circulating the publication to the American National Red Cross in Washington.

subfiles.about: Official handbook outlining the postwar reorganization, educational philosophy, civic objectives, and student activities of the Japanese Junior Red Cross.
subfiles.from: Japanese Junior Red Cross (with American Junior Red Cross Adviser)
subfiles.summary: Published in September 1947 with paper and guidance provided by the American Junior Red Cross, this handbook defines the structure and mission of the Japanese Junior Red Cross under democratic educational reforms aligned with the new Constitution of Japan. It details membership eligibility, a five-yen annual membership fee to be self-earned by students to teach civic duty, and the parliamentary organization of school corps and sub-corps directed by elected student officers. Practical service activities emphasize community hygiene, hospital aid, and an international school correspondence album exchange to foster world understanding and peace.
